args.message: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
Fixes the nightly build failure: `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`.

## Verification
- Example: `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` now correctly returns `2.66` (banker's rounding), matching the test expectation.
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed.

The bug is clear: `src/money.py` docstring says banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212, but the code uses `ROUND_HALF_UP`. The test confirms: `2.665` must round to `2.66` (half-even), but half-up gives `2.68`.

I'll create a branch and commit the fix:
transcript.reasoning_content:
The fix: change ROUND_HALF_UP to ROUND_HALF_EVEN in src/money.py. Verify test expectations: 2.675 quantize to 2.68 — note Decimal("2.675") is exact decimal 2.675, half-even rounds to 2.68 (since 2.67 vs 2.68, half way, even digit... 2.67 is odd last digit (7), 2.68 even (8), so half-even → 2.68 ✓). 2.665 → 2.66 (6 even) ✓. Also half-up would give 2.68 for 2.665, failing the test. So fix is correct.

Create branch, commit, run CI, wait, then open PR with reviewer alex.
